summary: GATE A: PASS. The PainterIO.Core simulation (contract sections 3-10) is complete and green in both worlds. No stub is left: no NotImplementedException and no 'STUB by A1' remain under Assets/Scripts/Core. Results: the dotnet run is 270/270 executed and green, and the 2 explicit BotReport cases pass when run on their own (272/272). Unity 6000.3.23f1 EditMode through tools/unity.ps1 gives JUnit tests=271, failures=0, errors=0, skipped=2 (the 2 explicit cases), so 269 executed, with no CS warning in the Editor log. tools/verify.ps1 -Agent gate gives PASS dotnet, PASS editmode, OVERALL PASS (docs/verify_last.txt). The counts agree: the one test of difference is Capture_NoGridSizedAllocationPerCall, which compiles only outside Unity. Unity runs 10 bot seeds instead of 50 and asserts only the invariants. The 6-seed audit fuzz gives identical event totals under Unity Mono and .NET 9 CoreCLR (Exit=245 Return=227 Cut=10 SparkCaught=8 LassoPocket=8 LassoCrossNoCharge=76 RingPicked=10, wallTicks=508), so the sim also replays the same across these two runtimes. GATE CHANGES. (1) Unity-only red test: AuditTests.Determinism_RoamingFuzz... ran 2 seeds in Unity, but its non-vacuity floors (for example Cut > 5) were calibrated on 6 seeds, and Unity got Cut = 5. The test was wrong for Unity, not the sim. It now runs the same 6 seeds everywhere and no floor was lowered (5.7 s in the Editor). (2) Root-cause fix of the open defect that A4 and A6 reported: Geo.ProperIntersect now applies its 1e-12 |db| rounding band to the moving segment's END as well as its start. An end in the band counts as reaching the line at a1 (ta = 1). A6's internal Trail.ProperCrossing wrapper is removed, so Trail.SelfCrossings and LoopErase call Geo.ProperIntersect as contract 5.4 says, and BotSenses.CrossesTrail gets the fix too. The formulas are A6's, bit for bit: the bot target statistics are identical to A5's report (lasso on: captures 26.90/26.66/18.88/32.28, cuts 88 %, Spark kills 66 %, TimeUp 94 %, coverage 38.5 %). New unit test Geo_ProperIntersect_EndInTheRoundingBandCountsOnce. (3) Perf visibility: new test Bots_Perf_FourPlayerTickCostDuringABotRound, and Capture_Perf_FullSizeBox now logs through TestContext so its numbers reach the Unity JUnit report. CONTRACT 10.1 CHECKLIST: every required id exists and passes. That covers the unit lists (Geo incl. the half-open rule, Arena, Rng, CellMask, OwnerGrid, GridRaster incl. TraverseFrom, GR-Edge at 30/60/144, RasterPolygon, CountInterior, LoopErase, Trail, LassoGeometry), C1-C7, every R id (R2, R4, R5, R9, R9b, R10, R11, R11b, R12b, R13b, R14, R15, R15b, R16, R17b, R18, R18b, R19, R19b, determinism), S1-S6 through SimTestKit.CrossRate at 30, 60 and 144 Hz with identical outcomes (A6 adds 7-rate checks), and the bot targets plus invariants. Nothing was missing. EventCapHits == 0 is asserted after every tick by SimTestKit.AssertInvariants (all rule, scenario and audit runs) and by BotTests.CheckInvariants (all bot rounds). PERF (all budgets met). CaptureSolver on the full box (rim loop, 506 x 506 box, 230,704 captured cells): Unity Editor 2.40 ms average (min 2.18), dotnet Release 1.50 ms (min 1.19), dotnet Debug 3.0-3.6 ms; opposite-corner box 1.04 ms in Unity. Budget 3 ms desktop; Android IL2CPP (8 ms) is not measured. FirstContact on a 2000-point trail: 0.58 us per query on spread-out queries, 3.1 us when 84 % of the queries touch the trail, 7.8 us in a 12 x 12 u dense worst case (Unity), against a 5 us budget for a typical query. SelfCrossings 1.2 us. A 4-player tick during a bot round (60 Hz, 4 bots, lasso on, seeds 1-3, 7339 ticks with all four alive, bots included): Unity mean 13.3 us, p50 3.6 us, p99 407 us, max 1.57 ms; ticks that contain a Return average 438 us. dotnet Debug: mean 22-27 us, max 2.6-2.8 ms. Bot decisions: mean 3.2 us, p99 31 us. WHAT WORKS: R1-R20 and the section 6 event engine, with exact in-tick ordering, the tick-u convention, the closed-form spark with the epsilon shift, R13 races decided the same way across tick boundaries and rates, R18 conflicts, stolen home cells, lasso pockets, contested rings, ranking and FinalCells, determinism by StateHash. The section 7 one-flood capture is checked against an independent two-flood reference. The FirstContact and SelfCrossings spatial hash is in place. Bots meet every asserted section 9 target on 50 seeds in about 10 s. KNOWN LIMITATIONS. (a) The 4-adjacency Rim (section 7 step 5) leaves stair notches on diagonal edges. A head gliding along its own diagonal edge then makes empty Exit/Return pairs at about 30 Hz: harmless for the rules, but each costs one CaptureSolver call and they inflate PlayerState.Captures. Wave B views and sounds must ignore them (see needs). (b) The near-loop raster limitation of section 8 is accepted. (c) A pure touch of an old segment exactly at a tick end counts as a lasso crossing (5.1 half-open rule versus brief 5.2 on tangency). It can only happen on lattice-aligned scripted paths. (d) An R4 hold stops up to one step short of the inset line, so the stop point depends on the tick rate. (e) Android performance and flicker cost are unmeasured (B6 probe). CONTRACT DEVIATIONS (all reported by the owners and kept): see contract_issues. API ADDITIONS (consolidated from all reports): see api_additions.

contract_issues: 5.1 Geo.ProperIntersect: the gate applied the symmetric rounding band that A4 and A6 asked for (an end a1 within 1e-12 |b1 - b0| of b's line counts as reaching it at a1: ta = 1, tb = projection of a1). Contract text to add to 5.1 so the half-open rule holds under rounding.

Section 6 text is behind four A6 fixes that are kept, all limited to rounding-sized windows: on the last tick, visit entries up to uEnd + 1e-9 are clamped to uEnd, and a catch with t_c in (RoundDuration - eps, RoundDuration] fires at uEnd in the TimeUp group (brief 6.4: the events of the final instant resolve first); pickup contact bounds are shifted by eps / dt for simultaneity (candidate times unchanged); step a drops a return whose own u is strictly after its own SparkCatch candidate in the same group (R13: t_r >= t_c + eps means eliminated).

5.1 half-open rule versus brief 5.2 'une tangence ... ne suffit pas': a head that lands exactly on an old segment at a tick end and then runs along it or turns back spends the charge and gets a pocket. This needs lattice-aligned scripted paths with TurnRateDeg 0 (measure zero in play). User decision (A6 proposes deciding a crossing on departure).

Section 7 step 5 (4-adjacency Rim) and section 6 step a ('Captures++' per returner): diagonal own edges keep stair notches, so a head gliding along them makes empty Exit/Return pairs at about 30 Hz (67 pairs in 2 s in R7_GlidingAlongAnOwnDiagonalEdgeFlickersHarmlessly). Captures counts them, and each costs one CaptureSolver call. User decision: count Captures only for Returns with Cells.Length > 0, or switch to an 8-adjacency rim. The A5 bot metrics already count only returns that captured cells.

R4 hold versus brief 2.3: Arena.Step returns p0 on a hold, so a held head stops up to one full step short of the inset line (0.2 u at 30 Hz, 0.1 u at 60 Hz). Its trail and captures near the wall depend slightly on the tick rate. Suggested: step to the inset line, then hold (A6).

10.1 RasterPolygon 'full raster vs area + perimeter * CellSize within 5 %' cannot hold for an axis-aligned square of side 4 (the supercover is (side + CellSize)^2, -5.5 %). The test asserts exact counts for axis-aligned squares and the 5 % tolerance from side 7.25 and for a rotated side-4 square. Suggested wording: 'area + perimeter * CellSize / 2 within 5 %' or 'side >= 6 u' (A2).

5.4 / R11 sCut: read literally it depends on segment subdivision, hence on the tick rate (a touch within 3.5e-5 u of a vertex, or an overlap at uMin). A3 drops a segment's start vertex when the previous segment is strictly closer, so sCut is subdivision independent; the three named behaviours are unchanged. Suggested wording: 'the closest exposed point of each pass in contact'.

Section 7 step (iii) is implemented as a multi-source scanline span fill instead of a BFS (same reachable set, checked against a two-flood reference on C1-C7 and 325 random cases); its seeds also include non-own trail cells on the border of a grid-clamped B (A2).

Section 6 readings by A4 (kept): the step-a stolen-home exit applies only when the current cell was taken by a capture of that group; step c also re-validates the victim's Trail.Version (R18b); a mid-tick round end freezes the state at uG; eliminated players get Home = true and Pos at the elimination point; random rings keep the whole ring disc inside the arena; SimEvent.Margin is clamped at 0; the round's player count is controllers.Length (the SimConfig is cloned).

Section 9 readings by A5 (kept): uncharged bots detour to avoid crossing their own trail on the return (otherwise R8 loop erase captures almost nothing); edge point E skips holes shorter than 1 u (rim notches); AttackChance is drawn once per enemy exit; a 0.1-0.6 s home dwell after each return; score noise and transit penalty in the direction choice. Presets retuned: Balanced MinOut/MaxOut/MaxTrailLength 4.5/10/34, Greedy 5.5/13/45 (others as in 5.7).

Version semantics (A1, A2): CellMask.Version and OwnerGrid.Version increment on content changes only; RasterPolyline / RasterPolygon add to their output and never clear it; OwnerGrid.Set(index, Void) throws. Arena.Step takes the outward normal at p0 + d (A1).
10.1 S6 'SparkCaught time = t_cut + (L(t_c) - s_cut) / SparkSpeed' is the closed form itself; the S6 test also asserts the independent arc-based time (A4).
open_issues: Counts: dotnet 270 executed and green, plus 2 explicit BotReport cases green when run separately (272). Unity EditMode: 271 tests, 269 executed and green, 2 explicit skipped. The gap is Capture_NoGridSizedAllocationPerCall (#if !UNITY_5_3_OR_NEWER).

B6's probe (ProbePerf) must measure it, including the diagonal-edge flicker cost (0.17 ms per tick in the Editor for one gliding player on a 12,720-cell territory).
